title: Mandodari
hook: Ravana's queen walks onto the battlefield, and says what no one else could say

segments.voice: Yesterday: the Aditya Hridayam. A hymn to the sun lifted Rama's weariness, and one arrow ended the war.

When the noise of victory dies down, the gates of Lanka open, and the women of Ravana's palace come out onto the battlefield. They've lost husbands, sons, brothers. They walk among the dead, weeping, until they find him. One of them comes forward and kneels by the body. She is Mandodari, Ravana's chief queen, Indrajit's mother. She has lost her son, and now her husband. Valmiki lets her speak over him at length.
screen: `THE GATES OPEN.` → `THE WOMEN COME OUT.` → `MANDODARI KNEELS.`

segments.voice: Her lament holds love and truth at the same time. She remembers who he was. You frightened the gods, she says. Indra himself feared you. The earth and the mountains trembled at your name. How could a man on foot, wandering in the forest, bring you down? Then she answers her own question, in two ways. First, she says Rama can't be only a man. In Valmiki's words, as she grieves, he must be the eternal, the supreme, Vishnu himself, come in human form. A queen of Lanka is the one who says it out loud, over her husband's body. Then she turns to Ravana's own part in it, gently and without flinching. Long ago, she says, you conquered your senses, and with that discipline you conquered the three worlds. Now it's as if your senses remembered, and took their revenge. Your desire for Sita did what no army could. She says she warned him. She says Sita's faithfulness was a fire he couldn't hold. And then she simply grieves: her husband, her son, her life in pieces. She falls across his chest and weeps. Later tradition honored her. A well-known Sanskrit verse names five women of the epics whose remembrance is said to wash away wrongdoing, and Mandodari is one of them. Valmiki's portrait suggests why. She's loyal without being blind. She sees her husband whole, the greatness and the ruin, and she mourns him anyway.
screen: `YOU FRIGHTENED THE GODS.` · `RAMA IS MORE THAN A MAN.` · `YOUR SENSES TOOK REVENGE.` · `ONE OF THE FIVE WOMEN.` · then, large: `LOYAL WITHOUT BEING BLIND.`

segments.voice: Let someone you love who has real faults come to mind, perhaps someone you've lost, and see them whole, as Mandodari did. Breathe in with the love and out with the honesty, and let the two sit together without arguing.
Mandodari. Ravana's chief queen and Indrajit's mother, who grieves him on the battlefield, naming both his greatness and the desire that destroyed him.
Your line: loyal without being blind. The king still lies on the field, waiting for his last rites. See you then.

howItsDone: Some Hindus recite a traditional verse naming five revered women of the epics, the pañcakanyā, with Mandodari among them, and some say it in the morning; versions differ on one of the names.

original.note: Sanskrit Mandodarī: Ravana's chief queen and Indrajit's mother, counted by tradition among the five revered women.

trapdoor: what you thought: Ravana's queen was a minor character.
what it means: she speaks over Ravana's whole life: his greatness, his fault, and her grief.
what a scholar hears: tradition counts her among the pañcakanyā, five revered women whose remembrance is said to wash away wrongdoing.

chat.says: When Ravana died, did his wife just praise him, or did she blame him too?
options: Both: she praised his greatness and named the desire that ruined him.
Only praise: she called him blameless and put the fault on Rama and Sita.
Only blame: she listed his crimes and refused to grieve for him at all.
chat.meaning: Mandodari's lament holds love and truth at once. She sees Ravana whole, his greatness and his ruin, and mourns him anyway.

notes: Sarga numbers follow the common (vulgate) numbering; confirm.
Mandodari's identification of Rama as Vishnu, the eternal supreme self (often cited as vyaktam eṣa mahāyogī paramātmā sanātanaḥ): paraphrased; confirm.
The senses-taking-revenge image (indriyāṇi purā jitvā jitaṃ tribhuvanaṃ tvayā / smaradbhir iva tad vairam indriyair eva nirjitaḥ): paraphrased; confirm.
The pañcakanyā verse: versions vary (Sita or Kunti); the script says only that Mandodari is among the five.
The meaning of the name Mandodarī ('slender-waisted'): confirm.
